thread:
sam (support): FYI customer reported decrypt failures after key rotation when using their HSM-backed CMK + cross-cloud wrap. They see 403s from our runtime and no rewrap entries in our audit for the window 2026-03-18T10:22-10:30Z.
maria (security): Details? customer on AWS KMS imported key or AWS CloudHSM-backed key? Any evidence of RBAC/permission denied vs envelope mismatch?
sam (support): They imported a key material to AWS KMS (multi-tenant HSM-protected) and mirrored a copy in Azure Key Vault HSM. App does local envelope decrypt: get data key from KMS, use AES-GCM. After rotation we see KMS Decrypt returns AccessDenied for a small % of requests. Customer says they rotated in Azure first, then AWS.
kelly (infra): AccessDenied from KMS usually RBAC/grants or key policy. Can you paste the exact error log lines (obfuscated)? Also ask customer if they're using a fixed key version ARN vs alias — rotation might change key-id used by our routing.
sam (support): pasted log snippet:

```
2026-03-18T10:23:12Z runtime[serve]: encrypt: getDataKey failed: KMS.Decrypt AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::11111:assumed-role/redwood-role-session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:22222:key/abcd-ef01
request-id: 7a3c-xx-yy
```
ashok (eng-sre): Two things to check quickly: 1) RBAC/grant propagation lag after rotation if they re-imported key material or changed key policy, and 2) key-rotation semantics if they used "replicate-key" or re-created key with new ARNs. If some clients are still routing to old key ARN our audit may not show rewrap because the event is against other resource/tenant.
maria (security): For cross-cloud BYOK we recommend: keep a stable logical alias (our routing should honor alias), use KMS Encrypt/Decrypt for data key operations (not raw RSA unwrap), and use AES-GCM for payload with key derived via HKDF. Also avoid client-side caching of wrapped keys cross-region for 24h after rotation.
kelly (infra): Can you ask customer to run this preflight check and share output:

```
# AWS: list key policy & grants
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:22222:key/abcd-ef01 --policy-name default
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:22222:key/abcd-ef01

# Azure: list role assignments on key
az keyvault key show --vault-name FIN-KV --name byok-key --query "properties.keyUri"
az role assignment list --assignee <service-principal> --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/FIN-KV
```
sam (support): Customer ran list-grants, shows a stale grant for a service principal that was removed in their tenant. They also have some calls coming from region eu-west-1 routed to us-east-1 KMS alias.
ashok (eng-sre): That explains AccessDenied bursts. For missing audit entries: our ingestion pipeline de-dupes by request-id and may have dropped events if their KMS request-ids didn't match expected mapping due to cross-cloud replication. I'll run an audit replay for that window.
maria (security): Actionable recommendations to give customer now:
• Re-issue grants to the active service principals and rotate the alias to point to the correct key-id.
• Avoid re-importing key material across providers at the same minute — stagger replication and monitor propagation.
• Use envelope pattern where the KMS only encrypts the data key and keep a short (ttl) local cache.
kelly (infra): I'll check routing rules and alias resolution in the router. If clients hit a wrong region alias we should fallback to canary model not to old ARN. Moving to ensure alias->key-id resolution is synchronized.
sam (support): customer asked about recommended envelope algorithm because they currently use AES-CBC + HMAC separate — they want to move to a safer default.
maria (security): Recommend AES-GCM (authenticated) or AES-CTR + HMAC-SHA256 as fallback. For data key wrapping always use KMS native Encrypt (which uses AEAD where supported). If they need RSA-OAEP for legacy, ensure padding matches.
ashok (eng-sre): Also log note — add a preflight checklist item for "check for stale grants & SPN deletions" and a one-liner command we can run during onboarding.
sam (support): Customer is also requesting an official doc section about cross-cloud BYOK rotation ordering and recommended throttle windows. We don't have that exact wording in docs.
maria (security): I'll draft a docs PR. Quick draft items:
• Recommended rotation ordering: primary cloud first, replicate with 5-10m gap, verify grants in each cloud.
• Don't re-use key-ids; prefer alias references in config.
• Example IAM snippet for cross-account decrypt role + least-privilege grant.
kelly (infra): Putting a small terraform snippet here to add to docs:

```
resource "aws_kms_grant" "redwood_decrypt" {
  key_id = "aws:kms:...:key/abcd-ef01"
  grantee_principal = "arn:aws:iam::22222:role/redwood-runtime"
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}
```
